standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: We're equal inside; difference is wonderful. Thread E root for ages 3-6. Retrofit of the v1 library (was 72% single-mechanic) to v2. Builds on g03.

categories.strong-gentle: Strong and gentle (everyone can be both)

evidenceBase: Gender stereotypes form by 3-6 (Vihaan already sorts 'girl colours'); the window to counter them is now, via play not lectures
Ages 3-6 learn through drag/sort, build, voice and story, not 'tap the right card' (Megha: no dopamine machine; Aria: no WRONG buzzer)
Counter-stereotype exposure + naming the myth shifts young children's beliefs; parent co-play extends it into real talk

scenarios.hook: Lensy found some toys. Who can play with them?

items.text: A doll, for anyone who likes it
A tea set, only for girls

scenarios.relearn: Toys are for anyone who enjoys them, not for one kind of kid.

scenarios.hook: Vihaan says "trucks are boys' toys."

myth.why: A toy doesn't know who's holding it.

scenarios.relearn: Anyone can play with trucks, or dolls, or blocks.

scenarios.hook: A toy is feeling lonely on the shelf.
scenarios.setup: Say it loud so the toy hears.
scenarios.relearn: Saying "anyone can play" out loud makes it true on the playground too.

scenarios.hook: Match each kid to a toy they love.
scenarios.relearn: Kids love all kinds of toys; the toy doesn't pick the kid.

scenarios.hook: Build a toy box for the whole class.
scenarios.prompt: Drag in toys for everyone to share.
scenarios.relearn: A great toy box has something for everyone, and everyone may share it all.

scenarios.hook: Your friend says "you can't play with that, it's for girls."

options.text: Say "toys are for everyone" and play together
options.consequence: You both have fun; the silly rule disappears.

options.text: Put it down and feel sad
options.consequence: You miss out, and the rule wasn't even true.

scenarios.debrief: A kind, clear "toys are for everyone" is all it takes.
scenarios.relearn: No one can tell you a toy isn't for you.

scenarios.hook: "Dolls are only for girls."

myth.re: Boys can love dolls too; caring is for everyone.
myth.why: Playing at caring helps every child practise being kind.

scenarios.relearn: Boys who play with dolls are practising care, and that's wonderful.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what's YOUR favourite thing to play?
scenarios.affirm: Whatever you love is exactly right for you. Play is for everyone.
scenarios.relearn: Your favourite play is yours, no toy is off-limits because of your gender.

scenarios.hook: Sort: fair sharing, or not fair?

items.text: Everyone gets a turn with the ball

scenarios.relearn: Taking turns is fair; keeping toys from someone for being a girl or boy is not.

scenarios.hook: A toy and the fun it gives, match them.
scenarios.relearn: Every toy is a kind of fun, open to every kid.

scenarios.hook: "You play with the wrong toys."

myth.un: Some kids play with the 'wrong' toys.
myth.re: There are no wrong toys; there's just what you enjoy.

scenarios.relearn: There are no wrong toys for you.

scenarios.hook: A new friend is unsure if they can join the blocks.
scenarios.relearn: Inviting everyone to play is how good friends play.

scenarios.hook: Build a play corner where everyone belongs.
scenarios.prompt: Add a sign for the corner.
scenarios.relearn: A play corner for everyone says: welcome, anyone can play, take turns.

scenarios.hook: Megha-moment: ask a grown-up to play YOUR favourite with you.
scenarios.affirm: Sharing your play with a grown-up is the best, and they'll see toys are for everyone too.
scenarios.relearn: Play is to share; invite your grown-ups in.

scenarios.hook: Vihaan says "pink is a girl colour."

myth.re: Colours are for everyone; pink is just a colour.
myth.why: Long ago pink was even called a 'boy' colour, fashions change, colours don't have a gender.

scenarios.relearn: Every colour is for every kid.

scenarios.hook: Dress the kid in any colours you like.
scenarios.prompt: Pick colours for the outfit (any you like!).
scenarios.relearn: Any kid can wear any colour, you choose.

scenarios.hook: Sort: true, or silly rule?
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can like any colour; rules that ban a colour are just silly.

scenarios.hook: A boy loves his pink shirt but someone laughed.

yourLine.text: "Pink looks great. Colours are for everyone."

scenarios.relearn: You can cheer a friend for wearing any colour he loves.

scenarios.hook: Match the kid to the colour they chose, all happy.
scenarios.relearn: When kids pick their own colours, everyone's happy.

scenarios.hook: Someone says your favourite colour is "for the other gender."

options.text: Say "colours are for everyone" and keep loving it
options.consequence: You keep your favourite; the rule fades.

options.text: Pick a different colour to fit in
options.consequence: You give up something you love for a silly rule.

scenarios.debrief: Your favourite colour is yours to keep.
scenarios.relearn: No colour belongs to one gender.

scenarios.hook: "Blue is only for boys."

myth.re: Anyone can love blue, or any colour.
myth.why: Colours are just light and fun, not rules.

scenarios.relearn: Blue, pink, green, all colours are for all kids.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what colour makes YOU happy?
scenarios.affirm: That's your colour, and it's a perfect choice. No colour is off-limits.
scenarios.relearn: Your favourite colour is a happy, free choice.

scenarios.hook: Sort the crayons, who can use them?
scenarios.relearn: Every crayon is for every kid.

scenarios.hook: You're choosing a balloon at a party.
scenarios.setup: The seller asks which you'd like. Say:
scenarios.relearn: You choose what you love, not what a rule says.

scenarios.hook: Paint a rainbow room for the whole class.
scenarios.relearn: A room for everyone has all the colours, shared by all.

scenarios.hook: "Wearing the wrong colour is embarrassing."

myth.un: Wearing the 'wrong' colour for your gender is embarrassing.
myth.re: There's no wrong colour; wear what you love proudly.

scenarios.relearn: Wear your favourite colour proudly.

scenarios.hook: Anyone can do these. Match the kid to the activity.
scenarios.relearn: Climbing, cooking, leading, anyone can do any of it.

scenarios.hook: "Girls can't climb high."

myth.re: Girls can climb just as high; bodies grow strong with practice.

scenarios.relearn: Girls can climb, run and jump as high as anyone.

scenarios.hook: A girl is unsure if she can lead the game.

yourLine.text: "You'd be a great leader, go for it!"

scenarios.relearn: Anyone can be the leader; cheering each other helps.

scenarios.hook: Who can do these jobs? Sort it.
scenarios.relearn: Doctor, nurse, anyone can be anything (more in Can-Do Kids).

scenarios.hook: "Boys can't cook."

myth.re: Boys can be wonderful cooks; cooking is for everyone.
myth.why: Many top chefs are men; cooking is a skill, not a gender.

scenarios.relearn: Anyone can cook, and it's a great skill to have.

scenarios.hook: The group says only boys can be the team captain.

options.text: Say "anyone can be captain" and pick fairly
options.consequence: A great captain is chosen on skill, not gender.
A good captain gets left out for no reason.

scenarios.debrief: Captains are picked for being good leaders, not for being boys.
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can lead the team.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what do YOU want to try?
scenarios.affirm: You can absolutely try that. Anyone can.
scenarios.relearn: Your dreams aren't fenced in by being a girl or a boy.

scenarios.hook: A boy wants to join the dancing.
scenarios.relearn: Boys can dance beautifully; anyone can join in.

scenarios.hook: Match each kid to what they're great at.
scenarios.relearn: Kids are great at all sorts of things, no gender required.

scenarios.hook: "Girls aren't good at maths."

myth.re: Girls are great at maths; it's a skill anyone grows.
myth.why: Ability comes from practice, not gender.

scenarios.relearn: Anyone can be brilliant at maths with practice.

scenarios.hook: Sort: anyone can, or silly rule?

items.text: A girl can fix a bike

scenarios.relearn: Sewing, fixing, anyone can learn anything.

scenarios.hook: Build a 'things I can try' chart.
scenarios.relearn: Your 'can-try' list is as long as you want; nothing's off-limits.

scenarios.hook: Aria-moment: is it okay for YOU to be the loud, leading one?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, it is. Big voices and leading are for you too.
scenarios.relearn: Leading and being heard are for every kid, including quiet 'good girls'.

scenarios.hook: You want to try something new that people call 'not for you'.

yourLine.text: "I can try anything I want to."

scenarios.relearn: Saying "I can try" is the start of every new skill.

scenarios.hook: Vihaan says "big boys don't cry."

myth.re: Everyone cries; tears are for every kid.
myth.why: Feelings aren't a gender (see Feelings Friends).

scenarios.relearn: Crying is okay for boys and girls; it helps big feelings out.

scenarios.hook: Strong and gentle, who can be each?
scenarios.relearn: Every kid can be both strong AND gentle.

scenarios.hook: A boy is holding back tears so he looks 'tough'.
scenarios.setup: Let him know it's okay. Say:
scenarios.relearn: Helping a friend let tears out is a strong, kind thing to do.

scenarios.hook: "Girls are too gentle to be strong."

myth.un: Girls are too gentle to be strong.
myth.re: Girls can be strong AND gentle, both at once.
myth.why: Strength and gentleness live in everyone.

scenarios.relearn: You can be gentle and strong; they're not opposites.

scenarios.hook: A friend fell and is crying. Others say "don't be a baby."

options.text: Help them up and say "it's okay to cry"
options.consequence: They calm down; you were the kind one.
They feel worse and more alone.

scenarios.debrief: Comforting a crying friend is the strong, brave choice.
scenarios.relearn: Kindness when someone cries is real strength.

scenarios.hook: Match the feeling to who's allowed it. (Trick: everyone is!)
scenarios.relearn: Every feeling is okay for every kid.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: can you be both gentle and strong?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, you can be both, and you already are.
scenarios.relearn: You hold both gentle and strong inside you.

scenarios.hook: "Boys have to be tough all the time."

myth.un: Boys must be tough all the time.
myth.re: Boys can be soft, scared, silly and gentle too.
myth.why: No one is tough every minute; that's not real.

scenarios.relearn: Boys get to feel everything, not just 'tough'.

scenarios.hook: You feel a big feeling and want to let it out.
scenarios.relearn: Naming a feeling out loud helps it feel smaller.

scenarios.hook: Sort: kind-strong, or unkind?

items.text: Carrying a heavy bag for a friend

scenarios.relearn: Real strength is kind; pushing and teasing are just unkind.

scenarios.hook: Build a superhero who is BOTH strong and gentle.
scenarios.relearn: The best heroes are strong AND gentle, like you can be.

scenarios.hook: Think of a time you were gentle with someone.
scenarios.affirm: That gentleness is a strength you carry. Use it lots.
scenarios.relearn: Gentleness is something to be proud of.

scenarios.hook: We're same inside, different outside. Sort these.

items.text: We all have a beating heart

scenarios.relearn: Inside we're alike; outside we're different, and that's wonderful.

scenarios.hook: "Being different is bad."

myth.re: Being different is wonderful; it makes the world interesting.
myth.why: Imagine if everyone were the same, how dull!

scenarios.relearn: Different is wonderful, not wrong.

scenarios.hook: Match the difference to why it's lovely.

pairs.right: So many ways to say hello
Everyone is one of a kind

scenarios.relearn: Our differences add colour to the world.

scenarios.hook: "Fair skin is prettier."

myth.un: Fair skin is prettier than dark skin.
myth.why: Beauty comes in every shade (Dark is Beautiful).

scenarios.relearn: All skin colours are lovely; no shade is 'better'.

scenarios.hook: Build a class photo with all kinds of kids.
scenarios.relearn: A real class is wonderfully different, and every kid belongs.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what makes YOU one of a kind?
scenarios.affirm: That's a wonderful part of you. Nobody else is just like you.
scenarios.relearn: Your differences make you, you, and that's a gift.

scenarios.hook: A new kid speaks a different language and looks unsure.

options.text: Smile and teach each other a word
options.consequence: You make a friend and learn something new.
You both miss out on a friend.

scenarios.debrief: Difference is the start of something interesting, not a reason to stay away.
scenarios.relearn: A kid who's different from you can be a wonderful friend.

scenarios.hook: Sort: kind about difference, or unkind?

items.text: "I love your different lunch, can I try?"
"Teach me a word in your language!"

scenarios.relearn: Being curious-and-kind about difference beats teasing it.

scenarios.hook: "Everyone should be the same."

myth.un: Everyone should look and be the same.
myth.re: We're all different, and that's exactly right.
myth.why: Same-inside, different-outside is the truth of people.

scenarios.relearn: We don't all have to be the same; difference is normal and good.

scenarios.hook: Same inside! Match each kid to the same feeling.

pairs.left: A tall kid and a short kid

pairs.right: Both feel proud when they try

scenarios.relearn: However different outside, we share the same feelings inside.

scenarios.hook: Think of a friend who's different from you.
scenarios.prompt: What do you like about them?
scenarios.affirm: Their difference is part of why they're great. Difference is wonderful.
scenarios.relearn: Differences are reasons to like someone, not avoid them.

scenarios.hook: Someone teases a friend for looking different.
scenarios.relearn: You can speak up kindly when someone is teased for being different.

scenarios.hook: "You can't play with us, you're a girl."

options.text: Say "that's not fair, anyone can play"
options.consequence: Most kids agree; the game gets bigger and better.
You miss out, and the unfair rule stays.

scenarios.debrief: "Anyone can play" is fair, and it makes games more fun.
scenarios.relearn: No one should be left out of play for being a girl or boy.

scenarios.hook: A kid is standing alone, not included.
scenarios.setup: Be the one who invites them. Say:
scenarios.relearn: A simple "come play" includes someone and makes a friend.

scenarios.hook: Sort: fair friend, or not?

items.text: Only picks boys for the team

scenarios.relearn: Fair friends share and include everyone.

scenarios.hook: "Boys and girls can't be friends."

myth.un: Boys and girls can't be friends.
myth.re: Boys and girls make wonderful friends.
myth.why: Kindness, not gender, makes a friend.

scenarios.relearn: Anyone can be friends with anyone.

scenarios.hook: Match the fair move to the happy result.

pairs.left: Pick teams by skill, not gender

scenarios.relearn: Fair play makes everyone happier.

scenarios.hook: Your team is only choosing boys for the running race.

options.text: Say "let's pick the fastest, anyone can run"
options.consequence: A fast girl joins and helps the team.
A great runner is left out for no reason.

scenarios.debrief: Pick people for what they can do, not their gender.
scenarios.relearn: Anyone can race; fair teams pick on skill.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: have you ever felt left out?
scenarios.affirm: That feeling is why we include everyone. You can be the one who does.
scenarios.relearn: Remembering how being left out feels helps us include others.

scenarios.hook: You see a friend being left out for being a girl.
scenarios.relearn: Standing up for a left-out friend is a brave, fair thing.

scenarios.hook: Sort: includes everyone, or leaves out?
scenarios.relearn: The best play includes everyone.

scenarios.hook: "Some kids just don't belong."

myth.why: Everyone deserves a place to play and friends.

scenarios.relearn: Every single kid belongs.

scenarios.hook: Build the rules for a fair playground.
scenarios.relearn: Fair playground rules: everyone plays, take turns, be kind, leave no one out.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: who could YOU include tomorrow?
scenarios.affirm: That's a kind plan. You can make someone's day with one invite.
scenarios.relearn: You can choose to include someone, every day.

scenarios.hook: "Only boys can be brave."

myth.re: Bravery is for everyone; girls are brave too.
myth.why: Brave means trying even when it's scary, anyone can.

scenarios.relearn: Every kid can be brave.

scenarios.hook: A boy wants to hug his friend goodbye but worries it's 'not for boys'.

options.consequence: You both feel happy and close.

options.text: Tell him hugs aren't for boys
options.consequence: He hides his warmth; that's a shame.

scenarios.debrief: Warmth and hugs are for everyone who wants them.
scenarios.relearn: Boys can be warm and affectionate too.

scenarios.hook: A friend is shy about their family being different.
scenarios.relearn: All families are different and good (see My Family Garden).

scenarios.hook: Capstone: you're picking who plays. The group wants to leave one kid out.

options.consequence: The whole group has more fun together.

options.text: Go with the group and leave them out
options.consequence: One kid is sad, and you feel off about it.

scenarios.debrief: Including everyone is the fairest, kindest, most fun choice.
scenarios.relearn: You can be the one who makes sure everyone belongs.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: same inside, different outside. How does that feel to know?
scenarios.affirm: It's a lovely truth: we're all alike where it counts, and special in our own ways.
scenarios.relearn: We're equal inside and wonderfully different outside.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what will you carry from today?
options: I can be strong and gentle
scenarios.affirm: Carry that everywhere. You're going to make play fair and kind.
scenarios.relearn: Toys, colours and dreams are for everyone; difference is wonderful.
